extraction.name: MMStar
extraction.description: An elite vision-dependent multi-modal benchmark for evaluating large vision-language models, comprising 1,500 human-curated samples spanning 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, designed to minimize visual-unnecessary samples and data leakage.
extraction.creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Samples were collected from six existing multimodal benchmarks, first filtered by an automated pipeline using LLM inspectors to remove visually unnecessary or leaked samples, then manually reviewed by three experts and curated into a final set of 1,500 samples.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data source consists of samples drawn from six existing benchmarks: MMBench, SEED, MMMU, ScienceQA, AI2D, and MathVista.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The sample pool was filtered by retaining only samples with hit counts of two or fewer from eight LLM inspectors, then split into four difficulty categories based on 16 LVLM hit counts before final manual curation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline evaluated candidate samples with two closed-source and six open-source LLMs using 2-shot inference for open-source models to reduce refusals and standardize answer formatting; only low-hit samples were retained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts manually reviewed coarsely filtered samples to ensure visual dependency, coverage of capability dimensions, and advanced multimodal difficulty, then manually curated the final 1,500 samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Difficulty analysis was performed by tallying hit counts from 16 LVLMs and dividing samples into easy, moderate, hard, and tough categories to support balanced manual selection.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B, and 16 LVLMs for difficulty estimation
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan future expansion into a larger online test set and dynamic evaluation methods.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to improve fairness, reliability, transparency, and equitable evaluation of LVLMs by reducing misleading assessments caused by visual-unnecessary samples and data leakage.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Existing multimodal benchmarks are biased by including samples that can be answered without visual input and by unintentional leakage of evaluation samples into LLM/LVLM training data; MMStar is designed to minimize these issues.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Even the best evaluated model scores under 60 on average on MMStar, and the authors note future plans to expand it into a larger online test set and dynamic evaluation methods.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating the multimodal capabilities of large vision-language models, including measuring accuracy as well as multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage.

name.evidence: To this end, we present MMStar, an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans.

description.evidence: To this end, we present MMStar, an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline... Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded... Ultimately, based on the difficulty of the rough-filtered samples, strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.

Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks with an automated pipeline... strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We first choose two benchmarks [27, 21] focused on natural images and four centered on scientific and technical knowledge [51, 30, 20, 29] for our sample collection.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Finally, we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits, indicating that around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer... we tally the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Specifically, we employ two closed-source LLMs [41, 34] and six open-source LLMs [1, 42, 49, 3, 19, 43] sizing 20B or larger to serve as inspectors. These open-source LLMs are applied with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting... Finally, we only retain those samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process to ensure: 1) each sample’s answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: To expedite the manual selection of samples with varying difficulty levels for LVLMs, we tally the hit counts of all 16 LVLMs on the coarsely filtered samples and split them into four difficulty categories: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: After the coarse filtering with LLM inspectors, we further employ three experts to conduct the manual review process

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we use eight powerful LLMs as candidates inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage, including two closed-source APIs (GPT4-Turbo [34], and GeminiPro [41]) and six leading open-source models (e.g., LLaMA-70B [43], Qwen-1.5-72B [1], and Mixtral-8x7B [19])... Then we use 16 leading LVLMs (e.g., GPT4V [35], GeminiPro-Vision [41], LLaVA series [24, 26]) to gauge the difficulty of the samples

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM’s and LVLM’s training corpora.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: The existence of inappropriate questions and data leaking would lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal performance gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM... For research to be transparent and equitable, it is imperative to account for and mitigate such leakage.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: we have identified two primary issues: 1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples... 2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training... Both problems lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In our evaluation of 16 diverse LVLMs on MMStar, even the best model scores under 60 on average. In the future, we plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs’ multi-modal capacities... Based on MMStar, we evaluate LVLMs with Accuracy and two newly proposed metrics: multi-modal gain and multi-modal leakage.
